title: Dynamic Tokenization via Reinforcement Patching: End-to-end Training and Zero-shot Transfer
claim: A decoupled policy trained with group-relative reinforcement learning yields adaptive segmentations that extend hierarchically and transfer zero-shot to new models.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right; large training panel, stacked middle panels, dashed feedback loops
description: Four rounded panels read left to right. Panel (a), End-to-end training, is the largest. An input time series passes through a blue Patching Policy box that outputs boundary probabilities. G colored patch segmentations (Sample 1..G) feed an orange compression-constraint box. They then go through a gray sequence model to rewards R(1)..R(G), and an orange box gives the reward and advantage formulas. A dashed blue GRPG update loop returns to the policy. Panel (b) shows the sequence backbone and forecast head, with prediction versus target producing a task loss and a dashed green gradient loop. Panel (c) shows multi-level boundaries on a waveform with fine and coarse patch bars. Panel (d) shows a frozen foundation patcher producing boundary logits. These split into default and custom-compression modes, then feed a plug-and-play downstream model that outputs a prediction. Colored boxes and small time-series plots carry the flow.
caption: \model learns a patching policy $\pi_\theta$ decoupled from the main sequence backbone $q_\phi$. (a) Training: for each input sequence, the policy $\pi_\theta$ emits per-position boundary logits. We sample $G$ boundary sets, each representing a patching strategy of the sequence that the backbone $q_\phi$ consumes to produce a prediction. The negative task loss on this prediction is then the terminal reward for the corresponding patching strategy. Advantages are computed group-relative and $\pi_\theta$ is updated by GRPG. (b) Sequence model: encoder downsamples points into patches, a latent transformer models patches, a decoder upsamples patches back to base granularity (Appendix [ref]). A forecast head then generates the prediction to calculate the task loss. Backbone $q_\phi$ is updated through standard loss back-propagation. (c) Hierarchical: the same policy can be extended to emit multi-level boundaries in one shot, without having to plan on-the-fly using the hidden representations of $q_\phi$ throughout its forward pass. (d) Zero-shot transfer: after large-scale pre-training, learned patching policy $\pi_\theta$ can be frozen and used as a standalone module to produce boundaries for a new downstream backbone, optionally at a custom compression rate via top-$k$ on the boundary logits.
abstract: Efficiently aggregating spatial or temporal horizons to acquire compact representations has become a unifying principle in modern deep learning models, yet learning data-adaptive representations for long-horizon sequence data, especially continuous sequences like time series, remains an open challenge. While fixed-size patching has improved scalability and performance, discovering variable-sized, data-driven patches end-to-end often forces models to rely on soft discretization, specific backbones, or heuristic rules. In this work, we propose Reinforcement Patching (ReinPatch), a novel framework that jointly optimizes a sequence patching policy and its downstream sequence backbone model with reinforcement learning. By formulating patch boundary placement as a discrete decision process optimized via Group Relative Policy Gradient (GRPG), ReinPatch bypasses the need for continuous relaxations and performs dynamic patching policy optimization in a natural manner. Moreover, our method allows strict enforcement of a desired compression rate, freeing the downstream backbone to scale efficiently, and natively supports multi-level hierarchical modeling. We evaluate ReinPatch on time-series forecasting datasets, where it demonstrates compelling performance compared to state-of-the-art data-driven patching strategies. Furthermore, our detached design allows the patching module to be extracted as a standalone foundation patcher, providing the community with visual and empirical insights into the segmentation behaviors preferred by a purely performance-driven neural patching strategy.
